rationale: The buyer is students and indie devs on mid-range laptops — a group with genuine pain but notoriously low willingness to pay for tools, especially when they're already trying to avoid API costs. There is no clear autonomous delivery mechanism: any 'curated guide' service or local-model proxy requires continuous curation, hardware-specific testing, and hands-on support that can't be fully automated. The deciding factor is that both the buyer (price-sensitive individuals, not businesses) and the build (hardware-dependent, high-support) fail the autonomy and commercial-reality tests simultaneously.
solution_plan: N/A — this opportunity is recommended for drop. The target users are cost-sensitive individual developers who are trying to escape paying for AI tools; they are unlikely to pay for a service that helps them avoid paying for services. Any viable offering (e.g. a local-model setup guide with ongoing updates) would require constant manual curation as models change rapidly, making it high-touch to maintain. A solo non-technical operator could not realistically build and sustain this in an automated way.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity (score 4, floor is 6), willingness_to_pay (score 4, floor is 5), and operational_autonomy (score 3, floor is 7). Total 4.3 is below the 5.5 validate threshold — drop.
